title: Cephalic Phase Liver Priming
summary: Während der Appetitreaktion (cephalische Phase) wird der Körper auf die aufzunehmende Nahrung vorbereitet. In dieser Studie wird untersucht, ob im Rahmen der cephalischen Phase im Menschen eine Veränderung in der Leber messbar ist und ob diese vom sympathischen Nervensystem abhängt.

interventions.name: Presentation of a food cue with administration of Propranolol or Vitamin B3
Presentation of a neutral, non-food cure (control)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Applicable to all groups
• capacity and ability to understand study procedures and willingness to comply with them and provide written informed consent
• good German language skills
• Non-smoker

Applicable only to group 1:
• Established indication for liver biopsy as part of standard medical care
• Informed consent for liver biopsy obtained as part of medical procedure

Applicale only to group 3A:
• Having received a kidney or liver transplant in the previous 3 years

Applicable only to group 3B:
• Patients with planned or performed surgery which injures the subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve;
these surgeries include
• transthoracal eosophagectomy with gastric reconstruction with truncal vagotomy for patients
with esophageal cancer and
• Gastrectomy and reconstruction by simple esophagojejunostomy with Roux-Y with truncal
vagotomy for Patients with gastric cancer, cancer of gastroesophageal junction II/III
• Weight loss <5%
• No higher grade tumor induced stenosis of esophagus or stomach
• Olgivie Dysphagia score 0-1

Applicable only to group 3C:
• Patients with gastric erosive reflux disease
• Indication for laparoscopic fundoplication with Nissen/Toupet technique or such surgery <12
months prior

Applicable only to group 4:
• Patients chronically or acutely impaired sense of smell
Exclusion criteria:
Applicable to all groups:
• Serious or unstable medical illness preventing to attend three testing days
• Current alcoholism or consistent substance abuse
• Current and history of major psychiatric illness as defined by the DSM-IV criteria including eating disorders that would prevent the participant from executing the tasks of the experiment
• Medications that affect alertness (e.g., barbiturates, benzodiazepines, chloral hydrate, haloperidol, lithium, phenytoin, etc.) and any psychoactive drugs or anti-obesity agents
• Current use of Betablockers, Vitamin B3 or other medication interfering with lipolysis or sympathetic signalling to internal organs
• severely impaired liver function, indicated by Child-Pugh Score C
• Diagnosis of MASLD (Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease), confirmed with liver biopsy

Applicable only to group 1:
• Indication for liver biopsy is given due to suspicion of cancerous lesion in the liver

Applicable to groups 1, 2, and 3:
• Chronically impaired or absent sense of smell

Applicable to groups 2, 3, and 4:
• Cardial or vascular Comorbidities, including:
- AV-Block II. und III. Degree or Sick-Sinus-Syndrome
- High grade sinoatrial Block
- Bradycardia
- heart failure (NYHA I-IV)
- Vasospastic Angina
- shock
- Hypotonia
- pulmonary Hypertonia
• Contraindications against the use of Propranolol, Vitamin B3 or ASS not mentioned in other exclusion criteria of the study
• Pregnancy
• Nursing women
